newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ PM Bolger won't rule out minority government.
newsitem.headline: NZ PM Bolger won't rule out minority government.

text.p: New Zealand Prime Minister Jim Bolger refused to rule out forming a minority government after Saturday's general election.

"We shouldn't at this stage, as New Zealanders, rule out minority government...That may be the option that emerges over the next few days or next few weeks," Bolger said after his conservative National Party emerged as the largest single party.
Bolger said he would continue as caretaker prime minister until the shape of the next government became clear.
There was no need for uncertainty or instability, he said.

Bolger's National Party campaigned on its record of strong economic growth, but saw its support slide in the closing stages as opponents, especially Labour, attacked its record on health and education.
Televised projections showed Labour, economic nationalist New Zealand First and the Alliance would comfortably outnumber National in the new parliament, but coalition prospects remain unclear.
